title: Worksheet 2: Phishing Scams (V2.0)
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: Phishing is a type of cyberattack in which criminals send fake emails, text messages, or other messages designed to trick people into revealing sensitive information, such as passwords, credit card numbers, or personal details. Phishing messages often pretend to come from a trustworthy source, such as a bank, a well-known company, or even a friend or coworker, and they frequently create a sense of urgency, warning that an account will be locked or a payment is overdue, to pressure the person into acting quickly without thinking carefully. Many phishing messages contain a link that leads to a fake website designed to look exactly like a real one, so when a person enters their username and password, the information is actually sent directly to the attacker. Some warning signs of phishing include misspelled words, generic greetings like "Dear Customer" instead of a real name, suspicious sender email addresses, and links that don't quite match the company's real website address.

questions.text: According to the paragraph, phishing is designed to trick people into:
questions.correct: Revealing sensitive information such as passwords or credit card numbers
distractors: Buying software they do not need
Deleting their own files by accident

questions.text: According to the paragraph, phishing messages often pretend to come from:
questions.correct: A trustworthy source, such as a bank or a well-known company

questions.text: According to the paragraph, what is one warning sign of a phishing message?
questions.correct: A generic greeting like "Dear Customer" instead of a real name
distractors: The message arrives in the morning
The message is longer than one page
The message includes the company's phone number

questions.text: A message warns that an account will be locked within one hour unless the reader clicks a link. Based on the paragraph, why do attackers write messages this way?
questions.correct: A sense of urgency pressures people into acting quickly without thinking carefully
distractors: Accounts really are locked after exactly one hour
Long deadlines are against email rules
It makes the message easier to translate

questions.text: A student clicks a link in a suspicious email and types their password into a page that looks exactly like their school login. Based on the paragraph, where did that password most likely go?
questions.correct: Directly to the attacker, because the page was a fake copy of the real site
distractors: Only to the school's login system, as normal
Nowhere, because fake pages cannot collect text
To the student's own device, stored safely
